parole.significato: towel (small piece of cloth used for drying one's body, body parts, also dishes)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German dwele (< Proto-Germanic *þwahljōn < Proto-Indo-European *twak- (“to wash”), from which English towel), first mentioned in 17th-century dictionaries.

parole.significato: used to express, reinforce agreement or confirmation, especially in response to a question; yes
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German ja, first mentioned in 16th-century religious works, especially catechisms, in answers to questions about faith. parole.significato: stiff, hard, numb (having lost, partially or totally, the flexibility of motion, because of, e.g., the effects of low t…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German stīf, or from Old Frisian stīf, or from Middle Dutch stijf, all meaning “stiff, firm, immobile, hard, strong” (cf. German steif, English stiff). First mentioned in 18th-century dictionaries, stīvs has replaced stingrs in some of its meanings.
Borrowed from Middle High German tallörken (“little plate”), replaced by another borrowing, šķīvis, by the end of the 19th century.

parole.significato: file (block of coarse metal attached to a handle, used for removing sharp edges or cutting)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German vīle, or Middle Dutch vīle (“file”) (compare German Feile, English file). First mentioned in 17th-century sources.

parole.significato: doctor, physician (a specialist with a medical education who treats patients)
parole.testo: First mentioned in 16th-century translations, borrowed from Middle High German arste or Middle Dutch aerste, both derived from Vulgar Latin archiāter, from Ancient Greek ἀρχιατρός (arkhiatrós, “chief physician”).

parole.significato: dish, plate (round, rarely oval, usually flat bowl for serving food; its contents)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German schive (“disk, round plate, dish”), or maybe from Middle Dutch schijf or an East Frisian word (compare Saterland Frisian Schieuwe, Skieuwe; also compare German Scheibe). parole.significato: school (institution of learning, usually of lower or intermediate level; also a special or specific institution of lear…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German schōle, or from Middle Dutch schole, both also borrowings from Late Latin scola, schola (“lecture; school”), itself borrowed from Ancient Greek σχολή (skholḗ). In Latvian, this borrowing is first mentioned in 16th-century texts and 17th-century dictionaries.

Borrowed from Middle High German smuk, smuck “flexible, accommodating, pretty, nice” or from Middle Dutch smuc “pretty, nice, clean” (cf. German Schmuck “jewelry, ornament”), first mentioned in 18th-century dictionaries.

parole.significato: stork (large bird with long neck and legs and a long straight beak; fam. Ciconiidae)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Middle High German stork or from Middle Dutch stork, from Old High German storh or Old Dutch *stork, both from Proto-West Germanic *stork (compare German Storch, English stork).
